# agent

define and run agents

Define and run agents from the CLI, the dashboard, or on GitHub, Slack and other platforms.

## `agent list [--server <server>] [--workspace <workspace>] [--yes] [--json] [--cwd <cwd>]`

list local or server-owned agents

Without --server, one row per built-in and workspace agent. With --server, list the agent records and current versions owned by that Coder server.

- `--server <server>` act on your Coder server
- `--workspace <workspace>` with --server: the workspace to act in (default: the saved one)
- `--yes` with --server: connect to a server used for the first time without asking
- `--json` JSON output
- `--cwd <cwd>` workspace directory; default current

## `agent show [id] [--server <server>] [--workspace <workspace>] [--yes] [--json] [--cwd <cwd>]`

one agent in full: settings, integrations, events, tools

Describe one agent as it will run here, or its active version on a server: its settings, access and per-integration events.

- `<id>` the agent
- `--server <server>` act on your Coder server
- `--workspace <workspace>` with --server: the workspace to act in (default: the saved one)
- `--yes` with --server: connect to a server used for the first time without asking
- `--json` JSON output
- `--cwd <cwd>` workspace directory; default current

```sh
coder agent show coder  # what the built-in agent listens to and may do
```

## `agent init [id] [--integrations <integrations>] [--events <events>] [--access <access>] [--name <name>] [--description <description>] [--permissions <permissions>] [--match <match>] [--yes] [--json] [--cwd <cwd>]`

scaffold an agent folder in .coder/agents

Create .coder/agents/<id>/ with an agent.json built from the integration catalog, a system.md to write the prompt in, and one sample event per integration for `coder agent run`. Asks for the id, integrations, events, and access when run in a terminal without them.

- `<id>` the agent id: its folder under .coder/agents
- `--integrations <integrations>` platforms the agent listens to (see coder agent integrations list)
- `--events <events>` events that start tasks, applied to each integration that has them (default: mention)
- `--access <access>` read or write, on its platforms and connections (default: write)
- `--name <name>` display name used in replies (default: the id)
- `--description <description>` one line for agent list
- `--permissions <permissions>` engine permission mode (default: auto)
- `--match <match>` start tasks only for event text matching a regex, as event=regex pairs
- `--yes` skip the questions and take the defaults
- `--json` JSON output
- `--cwd <cwd>` workspace directory; default current

```sh
coder agent init  # answer the questions, id included
coder agent init triage --integrations github --events issue,mention --access read  # no questions
```

## `agent push [id] [--server <server>] [--workspace <workspace>] [--yes] [--json] [--cwd <cwd>]`

upload workspace agents to a Coder server

Upload one workspace agent, or every agent in .coder/agents when no id is given. The server creates a new immutable version only when its definition, prompt, or files changed.

- `<id>` the agent (default: every workspace agent)
- `--server <server>` act on your Coder server
- `--workspace <workspace>` with --server: the workspace to act in (default: the saved one)
- `--yes` with --server: connect to a server used for the first time without asking
- `--json` JSON output
- `--cwd <cwd>` workspace directory; default current

```sh
coder agent push helper  # upload helper
```

## `agent run [agent] [file] [--server <server>] [--workspace <workspace>] [--yes] [--wait] [--flow <flow>] [--task <task>] [--json] [--cwd <cwd>]`

run a recorded event through an agent, offline or on a server

Run a recorded platform event (AgentEvent JSON) through an agent. With --server it goes through your Coder server exactly like a webhook: real app, tokens, runner, and the reply is posted. Without it the engine runs here on the agent's prompt and this checkout, platform tools off, and the reply is printed.

- `<agent>` the agent id
- `<file>` the event JSON file
- `--server <server>` act on your Coder server
- `--workspace <workspace>` with --server: the workspace to act in (default: the saved one)
- `--yes` with --server: connect to a server used for the first time without asking
- `--wait` with --server: follow the task log here until it finishes, then print the reply
- `--flow <flow>` override the matched flow
- `--task <task>` a runner's form: run that server task here
- `--json` JSON output
- `--cwd <cwd>` workspace directory; default current

```sh
coder agent run helper sample-slack-mention.json  # offline: print what the agent would reply
coder agent run helper event.json --server  # for real, through the server
```

## `agent usage [--since <since>] [--by <by>] [--server <server>] [--workspace <workspace>] [--yes] [--json] [--cwd <cwd>]`

aggregate usage by agent, installation, or engine

- `--since <since>` period such as 7d or 24h, or milliseconds since epoch
- `--by <by>` agent, installation, or engine
- `--server <server>` act on your Coder server
- `--workspace <workspace>` with --server: the workspace to act in (default: the saved one)
- `--yes` with --server: connect to a server used for the first time without asking
- `--json` JSON output
- `--cwd <cwd>` workspace directory; default current

## agent integrations

the integration catalog: events and tool presets

The platforms an agent can listen to and act on: their events and tool presets.

## `agent integrations list [--json]`

list integrations with their events and tools

One row per integration: its id, the events an agent can wire, and every tool it offers; `show` splits the tools by preset.

- `--json` JSON output

## `agent integrations show [id] [--json]`

events and tools of one integration

Describe one integration: each event with what triggers it, and the tools each preset (read, write) allows.

- `<id>` the integration
- `--json` JSON output

```sh
coder agent integrations show github  # the GitHub integration in full
```
